clue.text: The tree's coming down, to begin with

parts.note: a fir is a tree, so 'the tree's' gives the possessive fir's
something coming down is about to fall, read as the phrase to fall

explanation.surface: A lumberjack announces that the felling of the tree comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'the fir's to fall', i.e. the tree is coming down; the apostrophe in FIR'S is ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for firstly, at the very start of a list or sequence.

clue.text: Amount of fruit by river

parts.note: a fig is a fruit
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A quantity of figs grown by a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum or number, as in a sales total, is an amount.

clue.text: About to set an electrical device

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to lay something is to set it down

explanation.surface: Someone is about to install a piece of electrical gear.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrically operated switch that opens or closes a circuit is such a device.

clue.text: Book is a guide of course-little time to go into it

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it, so the short time goes inside the steering device

parts.note: a tiller guides a boat on its course
hr is the short form of hour

explanation.surface: A guidebook for a racecourse, with almost no time to read it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like a casual aside, but it means the course a boat steers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping novel full of suspense is a kind of book.

clue.text: In favour of including the old part of the theatre

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the word for in favour of holds the old word inside

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in votes for
ye is an old form of 'the', as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

explanation.surface: Someone supports keeping the old section of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The entrance hall or lobby of a theatre is this part.

clue.text: Sweet cocktail ingredients

parts.note: liquor, alcoholic drink, is one ingredient of a cocktail
ice is the other ingredient of a cocktail

explanation.surface: A list of what goes into a sweet cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail ingredients' supplies both pieces, the drink and what chills it.
explanation.definitionFit: A black confection flavoured with a root extract is a sweet or candy.

clue.text: Decided to return Mr. Kipling's poem

indicators.note: returning sends the run of letters from Mr and the poem title backwards

parts.note: Mr is the abbreviation for Mister, taken as letters
'If—' is Rudyard Kipling's best-known poem

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to send a copy of Kipling's poem back to Mr Kipling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns the whole run MRIF backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A decided view is a resolute, settled one, unwavering in conviction.

clue.text: Where a bedouin may be meeting one on purpose

parts.note: a desert nomad may be living in a tent
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A desert nomad deliberately keeps an appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on purpose' reads as one phrase, but 'on' gives letters and 'purpose' alone is the definition; 'meeting' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or plan someone means to carry out is their purpose.

clue.text: Engineers twice beat up criminal

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the written run is read from bottom to top
twice means the abbreviation is written two times

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to drum is to beat

explanation.surface: Army engineers twice assault a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run RERE DRUM backwards to give MURD and ERER in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer is the gravest kind of criminal.

clue.text: Top dog ?

parts.note: a pile of stones marking a mountain top shares its name with a small Scottish terrier

explanation.surface: Who is the boss?
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of small Scottish terrier, and also a heap of stones set on a summit.

clue.text: Poet embraces bad caricaturist

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the poet's name holds the word for bad inside it

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
ill can mean bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A poet hugs a wicked cartoonist.
explanation.walkthrough: James Gillray was a famous Georgian satirical cartoonist.
explanation.definitionFit: James Gillray is a celebrated eighteenth-century satirical cartoonist, an example of the type.

clue.text: Part given to enemy ?

explanation.surface: A share is handed over to the foe.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourth part of something is one sense; mercy shown to a defeated foe, as in 'give no quarter', is the other.

clue.text: Magnificent sail ?

explanation.surface: A splendid piece of canvas on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal splendour is one sense; a small sail set above the topgallant on a square-rigger is the other.

clue.text: River Niger road development

indicators.note: a development reworks something into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Building a road along the Niger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River' looks like it belongs with Niger, but it is the definition; NIGER ROAD rearranges into the American river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is the river forming part of the US–Mexico border, an example of a waterway.

clue.text: Have it in mind to sing, perhaps ?

explanation.surface: Someone is considering bursting into song.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider an idea is one sense; to amuse an audience, singing being one way, is the other.

clue.text: Appoints main collector to get in money, perhaps

indicators.note: getting in means going inside, so the scrambled letters go inside the banknotes

parts.note: notes are one form of money, banknotes

indicators.note: a collector gathers things up into a new heap, so the letters of main are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chief tax collector is appointed to bring in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIN rearranges to MINA, which goes inside NOTES.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone forward for a post or office is to appoint or propose them.

clue.text: School! is not to have return game

indicators.note: to have a return means the word not is read backwards

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A school refuses to stage a rematch.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonbridge School is a well-known English boarding school in Kent; 'is' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Kent gives its name to a famous English public school.

clue.text: Number of ends, in more than one sense, for pussy ?

definitions.text: Number of ends, in more than one sense, for pussy ?

parts.words: Number of ends, in more than one sense, for pussy ?
parts.note: a cat has this many lives, so this many ends of life

explanation.surface: Counting how many tails or deaths a cat may have.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is said to have this many lives, and the whip called a cat has this many tails.

clue.text: He's as mad as a bull in a china shop

definitions.text: He's as mad as a bull in a china shop

parts.words: He's as mad as a bull in a china shop
parts.note: a bull in a china shop would break crockery, and a madman is a broken vessel in slang

explanation.surface: A man is compared to a bull rampaging among the crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A madman or eccentric is called this, and a bull loose among crockery would split the pots.

clue.text: Note club for some evening out

parts.note: a flat is a musical note lowered a semitone
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Someone notes which club to visit on a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening out' suggests a night on the town, but here it means smoothing creases.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned smoothing iron heated on a stove is used for pressing out creases.

clue.text: House painter in swindle ?

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of painters
an MP is a member of the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A house decorator caught in a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House painter' suggests a decorator, but it splits into the parliamentary member and an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: In old British slang a racket or confidence trick is called this, a fraudulent dodge.

clue.text: Subordinate gets less than a pound — takes gin, possibly

parts.note: under means below in amount, as in under five pounds
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of gin may be in another order

explanation.surface: A junior employee earns very little and turns to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A lowly person who takes orders from superiors is a subordinate.

clue.text: Spots the animals?

explanation.surface: Someone sees the creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Small dark marks on the skin are one sense; small burrowing velvet-furred mammals are the other.

clue.text: Sign that one will brook no going back ?

parts.note: a beck is a northern English word for a brook or stream

indicators.note: going back means the word no is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A gesture showing someone will tolerate no retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brook' looks like a verb meaning tolerate, but it is a stream, BECK.
explanation.definitionFit: To gesture to someone to come closer is to sign or signal to them.

clue.text: What has a navigator to do with this assembly ?

definitions.text: What has a navigator to do with this assembly ?

parts.words: What has a navigator to do with this assembly ?
parts.note: a navigator must con, or steer, a course, and the two words joined name a crowd or gathering

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why a ship's navigator is at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A large gathering of people, or the open space where crowds meet, is an assembly.

clue.text: Girl met Helen inside

indicators.note: inside says the name lies within the run of letters of met Helen

explanation.surface: A girl met Helen indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a woman's given name, so a girl.

clue.text: Print a quarter of Melville's work

parts.note: to type is to print letters
E, east, is one of the four quarters or points of the compass

explanation.surface: Printing a fourth part of one of Melville's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' looks like a fraction of a book, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Typee is Herman Melville's first novel, set in the Marquesas Islands.

clue.text: Cricketer's score ?

explanation.surface: A cricketer's total of runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielding position near the batsman on the off side is one sense; a unit scored in a game is the other.

clue.text: That top-hole place of mine

parts.note: top-hole is old slang for excellent, but here the top of a mine's hole, or pit, is meant

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of their excellent home.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface buildings and shaft top of a coal mine stand at the head of the shaft.

clue.text: Poet finds the lady a strain

parts.note: her refers to a lady
to rick is to wrench or strain a joint, as in a ricked neck

explanation.surface: A poet discovers that a woman is a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Herrick was a seventeenth-century English lyric poet, an example of a versifier.

clue.text: Game Hampshire runner ?

explanation.surface: A match in Hampshire involving a sprinter.
explanation.definitionFit: An international cricket match is one sense; a river flowing through Hampshire in England is the other.

clue.text: Duke writes in gushing fashion

parts.note: welling means springing or gushing up, as water from a source
the ton is an old word for fashionable society or style

explanation.surface: A nobleman writes effusively.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Wellington defeated Napoleon at Waterloo; 'writes in' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Wellesley was created the first holder of this ducal title, a famous British aristocrat and general.
